02 / THE RESEARCH NOTEBOOK

Where human
intent meets machines.

My research interests sit at the intersection of movement, signal processing, and intelligent robotic assistance.

RESEARCH VISUAL / EMG SIGNAL EXPLORATION
ILLUSTRATIVE WAVEFORM · NOT PATIENT DATA
THE HUMAN–ROBOT LOOP

Listen to the signal.
Understand the movement.

Muscles produce electrical activity. Sensors capture that activity. Signal processing helps us understand patterns that may inform robotic assistance. It's the kind of human-machine connection I want to keep exploring.

01 / SENSE02 / ANALYZE03 / INTERPRET04 / ASSIST

At Stevens, my ME-800 work explored integrated EMG patterns in lower-extremity wearable exoskeleton research. My earlier prosthetic-hand project introduced me to translating muscle signals into actuator commands.

03 / A LITTLE ABOUT ME

Engineer.
Researcher.
Always curious.

Not just a collection of technologies — a journey shaped by experimentation, teamwork, and an interest in how things work.

I'm a graduate robotics student at Stevens Institute of Technology, with a foundation in electronics and communication engineering. I enjoy the space where hardware, software, and human needs meet.

My interests span wearable and assistive robotics, autonomy, embedded systems, and applied AI. I'm open to robotics engineering roles, internships, research opportunities, and collaborations across the field.
